quote.text: Cities have the capability of providing something for everybody, only because, and only when, they are created by everybody.
quote.author: Jane Jacobs, The Death and Life of Great American Cities (1961)

macro.title: What It Means — VWRA, Global Bonds, Gold & BTC

reads.text: capped — the AI-capex tape is bifurcating and rising long yields press valuations.

reads.label: Global bonds (held)
reads.text: duration is the sore spot, long-end yields at multi-year highs; USD-hedged AGGU is the friend against a bid dollar.

stories.headline: Five Quiet Days, Then the Missiles
stories.dek: The Gulf pause the oil market had sold for five straight sessions ended in a ballistic-missile salvo at American forces in Jordan. Washington and Riyadh struck back inside Iraq, Trump promised “a beating,” and Brent leapt back above $90 in a single day. Oman’s twin-corridor draft is not unsigned now — it is rejected.

stories.headline: The Verdict Lands; the Ticket Is Yours to Tear
stories.dek: Spider-Man: Brand New Day opens in Singapore today with its critics' verdict already in — Certified Fresh at about ninety-one, but the lowest-rated of Tom Holland's four solo films. The box office, the one number not yet printed, lands over the weekend.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Portfolio Lens
stories.headline: The Verdicts Land, and Not as Priced
stories.dek: The interval closed overnight. The Fed held — a fifth straight — but with three dissenters who wanted a hike; Microsoft beat and Meta missed on the same night; and the barrel bought back its war premium (p3). The market had priced calm. It got the opposite.

stories.headline: A New Cabinet Sits, and Trade Gets an Energy Portfolio
stories.dek: Lawrence Wong's reshuffle took effect on 27 July, so this is the first news week under the new line-up — and its quiet signal is a name change. From October the Ministry of Trade and Industry becomes the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry.

stories.headline: The First Brake Comes Off
stories.dek: Since 28 July a private-property owner can buy a non-subsidised HDB resale flat the day the deal is done — the fifteen-month wait-out is gone. It is the first cooling lever loosened since the market turned.

stories.headline: Nvidia's China Share Falls to a Number: Zero
stories.dek: Jensen Huang told a Citadel audience the company has gone "from ninety-five per cent to zero" in China, and that US export policy "has already largely backfired." The licences came back this summer; the buyers did not.

stories.headline: Garmin Answers Whoop Without the Subscription
stories.dek: The CIRQA is Garmin’s screen-free band — Body Battery, Sleep Score, HRV Status, skin temperature, a ten-day battery — and its pitch is the one number Whoop cannot match: two hundred dollars, once, and no monthly fee.

stories.headline: Home Assistant Aims for the Non-Tinkerer
stories.dek: The 2026.8 beta’s stated goal is a Home Assistant “you don’t need to be technical to use.” The migrator’s fine print is quieter: from this release the companion app drops iOS 15, watchOS 8 and macOS 11.

stories.headline: The Anti-Bigness Watch
stories.dek: Nomos has made two new versions of its smallest watch — a hand-wound Bauhaus square just 27.5mm on a side — in a market that has spent a decade getting larger. A quiet act of counter-programming for the wrist, at a shade over two thousand dollars.

stories.headline: France Draws the Line at Fifteen
stories.dek: France has become the first EU country to ban under-15s from social media — no new TikTok, Snapchat or Instagram accounts from September, existing ones deactivated by year’s end. For a parent of an eleven-year-old the cutoff is two years off, and the evidence behind it is shakier than the vote suggests.

stories.headline: The Dinosaur They Spotted From a Boat
stories.dek: A new 210-million-year-old dinosaur was found jutting from the rock above a Zimbabwean lake — noticed during a boat survey, then dug out. It shared its world with a larger cousin, and it makes the Late Triassic of southern Africa look more crowded than anyone expected.

stories.headline: It’s the Feeling, Not the Headcount
stories.dek: A new study that uses genetics as a natural experiment finds loneliness itself drives poorer health — and does so more strongly than objective social isolation. The felt state, not the friend count, is what the body seems to register.

stories.headline: The Metric on Your Wrist, Aged Gracefully
stories.dek: A global cohort of hundred-marathon runners had their VO2max pulled from their own wearables — and sat above the population’s 95th percentile at every age band. The age-related decline in the number these devices surface can, apparently, be nearly flattened. Read it carefully.

stories.headline: The Autumn Calendar, Corrected and Confirmed
stories.dek: A correction first: BTS's four Singapore nights are real and sold out — this desk got that wrong last week. Then the season firms up, and the seats worth an alarm open next week.

stories.headline: The League That Beat the Galácticos
stories.dek: In Jiangsu, thirteen cities field teams of delivery drivers and schoolteachers, a ticket costs 9.9 yuan, and the stands hold sixty thousand. It has become the most effective consumption stimulus in China this year — and it is the exact opposite of everything Beijing spent a decade and a fortune trying to build.
